title: Web Doubler for the Outer Radial Segments of the Rear Pressure Bulkhead on High-Cycle ZEPHYR-24 Aircraft
abstract: Proposed bonded and riveted web doubler on the six outer radial segments of the rear pressure bulkhead, intended to restore the original inspection threshold on ZEPHYR-24 aircraft accumulating cycles far faster than the design assumption.

sections.reason: Operators flying ZEPHYR-24 aircraft on very short sectors are reaching 40000 flight cycles at around fifteen years of age, roughly twice the rate the inspection programme was built around. Two operators have reported eddy current indications on the outer radial segments of the rear pressure bulkhead web, both starting at the outermost fastener row where the segment meets the circumferential joint. Seven findings have now been recorded across the tracked high-cycle population of 96 aircraft, and each has cost an eight-day check extension while a repair was agreed. The interval has been halved by service information, which is not a sustainable answer for a fleet that will run for another decade.
sections.description: A bonded and riveted doubler is added to the forward face of each of the six outer radial segments of the bulkhead web, overlapping the circumferential joint by two fastener pitches. The superseded shear tie D5331135070611 is replaced, the outboard bracket D5331131182950 is re-drilled to the new pattern, and the vendor lug GIR251836-67 at the segment root is renewed. Clevis pins AGS566056-63 secure the doubler to the radial stiffeners during bonding and remain in place. Because the doubler footprint reaches the tailplane attachment area, the attachment lug CI558884-44 is disturbed and must be re-shimmed on removal. Access is through zones 143, 146 and 193 with the rear galley, the aft cargo lining and the tail cone disconnected. Drawings D53311318307 issue H and D53311387814 issue F carry the segment layout and the bond schedule.
sections.effects: Estimated mass increase of 13.6 kg per aircraft, all of it aft of the rear spar, giving a centre-of-gravity shift of about 0.18 per cent MAC that will need a weight and balance manual amendment. No electrical load change. The doubler is not interchangeable with the pre-modification bulkhead because the web is re-drilled during embodiment. If the substantiation holds, the inspection threshold returns to its published value and the halved interval imposed by service information can be withdrawn. AMM, IPC and SRM content for ATA 53-31 will require re-issue.
sections.embodiment_note: Retrofit only. Provisional estimate is nine days inside a heavy check with the aft cabin already stripped. No production cut-in is proposed because the current build standard already carries a thicker web.
sections.open_points: Pre-analysis must decide whether the tailplane front spar attachment work has to be embodied in the same shop visit, whether an aircraft already carrying an approved bulkhead web repair can be modified, and whether the aft fuselage access task can be shared with the tailplane attachment procedure rather than duplicated.

type_data.balance_impact: Aft mass addition, CG shift approximately 0.18 % MAC
type_data.production_impact: No production cut-in; the current build standard already carries a thicker web

issue.reason: The written stress position on jig registration against a doubled web is recorded, together with the embodiment order it imposes.

abstract: Proposed bonded and riveted web doubler on the six outer radial segments of the rear pressure bulkhead, restoring the original inspection threshold on high-cycle ZEPHYR-24 aircraft and sequenced against the tailplane attachment retrofit.
